description: Store ONE atomic fact in long-term memory: a single assertion, ideally one sentence (aim for under 250 characters; writes over 1500 are rejected). Split compound knowledge into multiple remember calls so each piece can be revised independently later. Use for durable knowledge about the user, their projects, preferences, decisions, and environment — not transient task state. If this contradicts an existing belief, find it with recall and use revise instead. Always fill source_ref with where this came from (session, file, URL) if known. If the fact describes code you just read at a known commit, also set source_commit (and source_path) so staleness checking can flag it when the repo moves past that commit.

basis.description: How you know this: user-stated (they told you), verified (you checked directly), reported (read in docs/code but not confirmed), inferred (your deduction). Sets confidence. Default user-stated

confidence.description: Numeric override for basis; rarely needed

importance.description: 1–10 salience: how strongly this should rank up and resist decay. Default 5 (neutral). Reserve 8–10 for durable, high-stakes facts (core identity, hard constraints); 1–3 for incidental detail.

kind.description: semantic = stable facts/preferences (slow decay), episodic = events/one-offs (fast decay), procedural = how-to/workflow (slow decay). Default semantic.

source_commit.description: Git SHA you read this code at; pins the fact for staleness checking. Omit for non-code facts.

source_path.description: Repo-relative file path this fact describes, if any.

source_ref.description: Where this came from: session id, file path, URL, utterance

subject.description: What the fact is about, e.g. 'user' or 'project:memharness'

valid_from.description: ISO 8601: when this became true in the world, if not now

name: remember
